questions.question: When does a large combination vehicle take the longest to stop?
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded vehicles. Less weight means the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: You are driving a vehicle built before 1998. How can you check if the trailer has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes to see if it has ABS.

questions.question: When connecting glad hands, match the colors. What color are service lines usually?
questions.explanation: Service lines are usually blue. Emergency lines are usually red. Color coding helps drivers connect the right hoses.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent rollovers?

options.text: Keep the load near the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, load your cargo as low as possible. Take curves and turns slowly.

questions.question: After coupling, how much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.explanation: Before a trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
Try driving on a slippery surface and see if ABS kicks in.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built after March 1, 1998 must have ABS. For older trailers, look under them for wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, what should you do?
questions.explanation: After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer. This is an important step in proper coupling.

questions.question: What color are emergency air lines usually?
questions.explanation: Service air line parts are coded blue. Emergency air line parts are coded red.

questions.question: What does pushing in the trailer air supply control do?
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs compared to empty rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over.
Are more likely to roll over.
Are just as likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: Trailers built before 1975 must have spring brakes. True or false?

options.text: True. They are required to have spring brakes.
False. They are not required to have spring brakes.
They cannot be driven on public roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: False. They are not required to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. If you park a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control on newer vehicles is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: Trailers made after what year must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.explanation: Trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Makes it easier to turn a large vehicle.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the top of the wheel in the direction you want the trailer to go.
Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
It depends on where you are backing the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the top of the wheel opposite to where you want to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, switch the wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What should the trailer hand valve be used for?

options.text: To check if the trailer and tractor are connected.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve, also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar, operates the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: Back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: What is off-tracking?

options.text: The front wheels follow a different path than the rear wheels.
All wheels follow the exact same path.
The load shifts during a turn.
The wheels hit a curb during a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front wheels follow a different path than the rear wheels.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking or 'cheating'.

questions.question: Combination vehicles are longer than other commercial vehicles. What else makes them need more road space?

options.text: They need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space because they are longer and need more room to turn and stop. Managing space is very important when operating a combination vehicle.

questions.question: How do you check that air reaches all trailers before driving?

options.text: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for escaping air.
Roll each trailer down a hill and test the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Before driving, make sure air reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build. Send air to both emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves at the back of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is flowing to the entire vehicle.
